topic: Earth's true shape (the geoid) and why it keeps changing
title: Earth Isn't a Perfect Sphere — Here's Its Real Shape
description: Earth isn't a smooth ball — it's a lumpy 'geoid' shaped by gravity, and satellites show that shape is actually shifting over time. Original AI-narrated science commentary exploring geodesy, gravity mapping, and why melting ice is subtly reshaping the planet.

beats.text: Earth isn't a perfect sphere — it's not even a smooth oval.
It's what scientists call a geoid: a lumpy, uneven shape defined by gravity, not geometry.
Mountains, oceans, and even underground rock density pull that shape in different directions.
And it's not fixed. Satellites tracking gravity shifts have shown Earth's shape actually changes over time.
Melting ice sheets move billions of tons of mass from the poles into the oceans.
That shifts Earth's center of mass and slightly reshapes the whole planet.
Even the planet's spin axis has wobbled measurably because of it.
So next time someone says Earth is just a ball, remind them: it's a living, shifting shape.
